In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of attribute-value extraction, a problem that is central to the construction of a large-scale knowledge base from the Web.
developing methods for extracting structured information from semi-structured data.
the design of scalable algorithms that can extract attribute-value pairs from semi-structured text.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system is the first to demonstrate that a scalable, general purpose attribute-value extractor can perform well on a large corpus.
our system can be scaled up to a large corpus of web pages and can achieve good accuracy.
our method achieves a high precision and recall on a large-scale corpus of semi-structured text.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general methodology for scalable attribute-value extraction, and have applied it to the task of extracting product information from e-commerce sites.
the best combination of candidate generators and candidate filters can handle 1B web pages with 1K machines in 6 hours, achieving F-measure of 70% compared to a hand annotated corpus.

we have designed and developed a scalable, parallelizable, and high performance framework for the task of attribute-value extraction from web pages, and that the system can handle 1,000,000 web pages in less that 6 hours on a cluster of 1,000 computers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the candidate generation phase is more important than the candidate filtering phase.
it is possible to extract attribute-value pairs from the entire web in a reasonable amount of time.
the candidate generation and candidate filtering phases are largely independent, so they can be implemented separately.
